why: A small open-air boxing ring in the Eden Plaza / Montezuma's Throne corner of Dogtown, ringed by stacked housing and a background crowd of outcasts, workers, kids and gym jocks. Vanilla's mq306 adds the ring's own cast on top: a referee, twelve spectator spots, two kids, and a pair of boxers in the ring - all only while the quest runs its fight and Angie's meeting. In our timeline nobody stages that job, so this proposal restores the venue's normal look: an evening bout in the ring (boxer_01 and boxer_02 at the two boxing workspots), the referee at the ring apron and the full spectator crowd at the ring's cheer spots, with the quest's VR-fight and ring-securing variants switched off.

open_questions: Check that the ring shows a calm local bout. boxer_01 and boxer_02 should box each other at the two ring workspots, the referee should stand at the ring apron and the crowd should cheer or watch - nobody hostile, crouched or on a combat spot.

Check that the 12 adult and 2 child spectators land on the ring-side spots. No community area node exists for #mq306_com_spectators, so entry-to-spot assignment is inferred from the spot names; note anyone standing in the wrong place or in a duplicate spot.
Check whether the two Barghest spectators (spectator_male_02, spectator_male_04) stay calm. They use kurtz grunt records; if they read as guards rather than fans, drop those two entries.

Check that the proximity re-issue fires at the ring. The anchor is the neighbouring open-world security area (61 m, no device exists at the ring itself); if the ring only populates on the first load, report whether a closer device (the access points about 45 m away) is needed.

Check the ring variants. Confirm the ring has no VR overlay with mq306_vr_fight=0 and no security fence with the decoration states at 0, and whether ring_collision=0 lets you walk into the boxers (if it does, try 1).

communities.why: The ring's referee in his match phase; his spot is a plain stand at the ring apron (stand_around__03), not a combat pose. No community area node exists for this spawner, so the entry-to-spot assignment is inferred from the spot names.

One of the two boxers vanilla puts in the ring. His only phase is 04b_meeting and his spot is a genuine boxing workspot inside the ring (boxing__01), so he reads as a fighter working the bout rather than as a talker: the referee, the crowd's cheer spots and the other boxer all point at a match.
The second boxer of the pair, one metre from boxer_01 at the neighbouring boxing workspot, so the two of them box each other in the ring instead of leaving one empty corner.

A local kid watching the fight from the ring side; his spot is the child cheer workspot. The catalogue tags the record 'combat' only because the record name contains the district name 'combat_zone'; the entry is a child spectator.
Second kid at the ring side, on the other child cheer spot. Same district-name role quirk as spectator_child_01.

Ring-side spectator of the mq306 crowd; the boxing-ring phase spots are the watching/cheering set, while her 'after fight' spots (lean, smoke, sit on the ground) belong to the aftermath and are not used.
Second female ring-side spectator of the crowd, same watching workspots.
A big gym jock from the plaza's sport crowd, watching the bout from the ring side.

An off-duty Barghest gun (kurtz grunt record) watching the fight. Vanilla placed him in this same crowd for the intro, so a Dogtown ring with armed locals is the venue's own look; the pose is a cheer/watch spot, not a combat spot. Rule 11a also puts combat records ahead of civilians when an area is capped.
Second big gym jock in the ring-side crowd.
Second off-duty Barghest gun in the crowd; same reasoning as spectator_male_02 - Dogtown locals with hardware at a street fight, watching from a cheer/watch spot.
One of the plain local spectators; his boxing-ring spot is one of the twelve watching poses (cheer, think, film on a phone, coffee, fries).
Plain local spectator of the crowd, watching from the ring side.
Plain local spectator; one of his boxing-ring poses films the fight on a phone, which fits a street bout.

Plain local spectator of the crowd, watching from the ring side.
Last of the ten male spectators; with him the crowd is 12 adults plus 2 kids for the 12 adult and 2 child ring-side spots.

variant_toggles.why: mq306_vr_fight=1 is the backdrop the Angie meeting uses while she talks V around; the intro's real fight - the ring's own match - runs with 0, and the quest returns to 0 afterwards. Keep the normal ring, not the conversation's staged overlay.
The intro clears both states when the fight is over (ring walkable, no securing fence), which is the venue's everyday look between and around bouts; only the quest's staged fight raises them.

proximity_wait.why: The ring drives no device of its own: its quest prefab holds only triggers, splines, workspots and prevention areas, and the five devices in input.json are Digimmortal's (mq306_pr_base, about 870 m away at high_peak), attached to this venue by phase inference only. The nearest real device in an always-streamed open-world sector is this monument-av combat-zone security area, 61 m from the ring centre (entity id 11206153359983598246, ref hash verified), in the same open-world community prefab as the ring's ambient crowd, so an 80 m proximity wait fires at the ring. Flagged in open_questions.
